topic: The Pulse of Rhythm: An Introduction to Music and Measure Theory
target_audience: Middle school students or beginner music theory enthusiasts

sections.title: The Prerequisite: The Metronome Pulse
lecture_lines: Music relies on a steady, consistent beat.
This pulse acts like a clock for musicians.
Think of a heartbeat keeping rhythm steady.
animations: Create five evenly spaced vertical white bars at #FFFFFF.
Flash each bar sequentially from left to right at #FF00FF.
Transform the five bars into a single horizontal timeline.
Place a pulsing dot moving across the timeline at #00FFFF.
Highlight the final timeline with a gold border at #FFD700.

sections.title: Grouping the Beats: The Concept of the Bar
lecture_lines: Music requires organization to stay together.
We group beats into rhythmic measures.
The downbeat signals a brand new cycle.
animations: Display three sets of four dots at #FFFFFF.
Group each set of four dots inside a rectangle at #FF00FF.
Highlight the first dot of each group at #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Time Signature: The Mathematical Fraction
lecture_lines: Time signatures look like math fractions.
The top number counts beats per measure.
The bottom number shows the note value.
Four-four time means four quarter beats.
The pie chart shows the measure's capacity.
animations: Write the fraction 4/4 in large white text at #FFFFFF.
Split the fraction into top digit (4) and bottom digit (4).
Highlight the top digit (4) in red at #FF4500 to show beats per bar.
Highlight the bottom digit (4) in blue at #1E90FF to show beat type.
Animate the two parts merging back into the whole fraction.

sections.title: Applying the Theory: Rhythmic Patterns
lecture_lines: Notes must fill the measure perfectly.
Different durations add up to the total.
Rhythm works like a musical puzzle.
animations: Display a sequence of quarter notes on a staff at #FFFFFF.
Group notes into patterns of four at #FF00FF.
Accent the first note of each pattern with a pulse at #00FFFF.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Living Measure
lecture_lines: Measures act as a shared grid.
They allow everyone to play in sync.
The whole band lands on one together.
animations: Animate a metronome moving back and forth at #FFFFFF.
Show musical notation flowing beneath the metronome at #FF00FF.
Sync the metronome clicks with the musical notes at #00FFFF.
